name: Movers and relocation companies

problems.words: Lots of enquiries on WhatsApp but most just want a price and disappear
quick_ideas: Ask every enquiry for move type, size and date first, so serious ones stand out
Offer a quick video survey slot, so real customers move forward.

workzap_build.text: WhatsApp enquiry intake that collects move details and photos and routes serious enquiries to the surveyor quickly.

problems.ask_first: Do most enquiries vanish right after you quote, or before you can even ask the details?
problems.free_stops: The intake questions and routing are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which enquiries share full move details before asking about price, so time goes to people closer to booking.
Keep one notebook list of open enquiries with one person checking it at set times, so fewer serious leads go cold.

problems.words: We reply late to enquiries and lose them
quick_ideas: Make one person responsible for enquiries during busy hours, so replies are fast
Look at last week's lost enquiries, so you see how long replies took.

workzap_build.text: Every enquiry recorded with follow-up reminders until it's booked or closed.

problems.ask_first: Are replies slowest during the day, or in the evenings and weekends?
problems.free_stops: Follow-up timing is set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare enquiry time with reply time for recent chats, so you see when delays are costing bookings.
Give one person each shift the enquiry phone duty, so new chats get answered during rush periods.

problems.words: Quotes based on photos are wrong and we lose money on the day
quick_ideas: Compare your last few quotes with actual volume, so you see how far off they run
Make quotes state clearly what's included.

workzap_build.text: A survey checklist and volume calculator by room that produces a standard quote.

problems.ask_first: Are quotes wrong mostly for large homes, or for all sizes of move?
problems.free_stops: The survey method and calculator are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which quoted jobs needed extra crew time or packing on the day, so underquoted move types stand out.
Give one estimator the job of checking photo based quotes against completed jobs weekly, so pricing improves from recent mistakes.

problems.words: Customers add items on moving day and argue about extra charges
quick_ideas: Get added items approved by the customer before loading, so there's no argument later
Tell customers at booking how extras are handled.

workzap_build.text: A move-day change form where added items are priced and approved by the customer on WhatsApp before loading.

problems.ask_first: Do extra items come mostly on home moves, or on office moves too?
problems.free_stops: The change-approval flow is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many jobs had extra items added at loading this week, so you see how often pricing disputes start.
Keep one written add on list with the crew leader on every move, so extras are recorded before the truck leaves.

problems.words: Breakages lead to angry calls and bad Google reviews
quick_ideas: Photograph valuable furniture's condition before the move with the customer present, so damage claims start from facts
Reply calmly to recent reviews.

workzap_build.text: Pre- and post-move condition photos per job, and review requests sent automatically to genuinely happy customers.

problems.ask_first: Is it mostly broken furniture, or mostly missing items?
problems.free_stops: The photo routine and review flow are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which breakage complaints came from packing, loading or unloading, so the weak part of the move is clear.
Give one crew member the job of checking fragile items against the job notes before departure, so avoidable damage is less likely.

problems.words: Two jobs booked on the same day with the same truck
quick_ideas: Keep one calendar of jobs with crew and truck assigned, so clashes are visible
Let one person book jobs.

workzap_build.text: A job calendar with crew, truck and helpers assigned, blocking double bookings and confirming helpers the night before.

problems.ask_first: Does the clash come when one person books, or when several people book?
problems.free_stops: The scheduling rules are set in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare booked jobs against truck assignments for the coming week, so clashes are caught before customers are promised the slot.
Keep all confirmed jobs in one booking notebook managed by one scheduler, so truck availability stays tied to each promise.

problems.words: We don't know profit per job after labour, truck and material
quick_ideas: Work out the real cost of last week's jobs, so you see which types pay
Note packing material used per job.

workzap_build.text: Job costing with labour hours, truck and materials used vs quoted, per job.

problems.ask_first: Do you track any cost per job now, or only the total at month end?
problems.free_stops: How costs are captured per job is designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each completed job's price with labour, truck time and packing used, so low earning move types become visible.
Give one person a same day notebook line for each job's crew hours and materials, so job earnings stop being guessed.

problems.words: Crew leaders collect cash on site and it doesn't all reach us
quick_ideas: Offer customers a payment link, so less cash is handled on site
Settle on-site cash the same day, so gaps are caught.

workzap_build.text: Payment status per job with on-site cash logged and matched daily.

problems.ask_first: Is the missing cash from a few crew leaders, or from most of them?
problems.free_stops: The settlement steps are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare cash collected on each job with cash handed in that evening, so missing site collections are spotted quickly.
Give one office person the daily handover of all site cash with one notebook record, so every collection has an owner.

problems.words: We don't know which channel brings the good customers
quick_ideas: Ask every enquiry how they found you, so you can compare channels
Note which channels turned into paying jobs last month.

workzap_build.text: Links and codes per channel showing which ads and listings bring paying jobs.

problems.ask_first: Do most of your customers come from referrals, from ads, or from Google?
problems.free_stops: How codes are set per channel is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which enquiry sources turned into actual moves this month, so you see where the serious customers come from.
Keep one source list beside the enquiry phone and make one person note it for every new chat, so comparisons stay complete.

problems.words: No repeat or referral system even though people move again
quick_ideas: Ask recent customers, with their permission, whether you may contact them later
List past corporate HR contacts you could reconnect with.

workzap_build.text: Follow-up messages to past customers who agreed, with referral reminders at the right time.

problems.ask_first: Do you hear again from past customers at all, or never once the move ends?
problems.free_stops: Message timing and content are planned in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many past moves led to another booking or referral this season, so you see where repeat work is leaking.
Give one staff member a weekly notebook page for past customers due to move again, so follow ups actually happen.

never_say: Anything on international household goods customs rules, duty-free allowances or prohibited items; suggest the destination agent or customs authority.
Help hiding items in a shipment or under-declaring.
Insurance claim outcomes or consumer law; customers' immigration or residency questions.
Covert monitoring of crew accused of theft.
Storing customers' addresses, numbers, ID copies or inventories of valuables. For lifting injuries, falls or truck accidents, emergency services come first.

sample_reply.person: We're movers in Dubai. We quote from photos, then on the day there's way more stuff and the customer won't pay extra. How do we fix this?
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, there are practical first steps, and the first steps are simple.
First, compare your last few quotes against the real volume moved, so you see how far off the photo method runs.
Second, get any added items approved by the customer before loading, so the extra is agreed, not argued.
What Workzap would add is: a room-by-room survey calculator for quotes and a move-day change form the customer approves on WhatsApp.

Shall I have a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're welcome to say no.
